rationale.complete: Round 1 done on the requested scope: card and dated predictions, Mathis A0 secondary test, synthetic validation on real call schedules (6 worlds + 3 post hoc fitness worlds, expiry sweep), 6 replication periods and 2 natives with per-period verdicts, variants (expiry, bin size, clock, choice form, cross-lab, first-time, touch class), estimates rows and a frozen, guarded confirm script (dry-run on stand-ins only).
rationale.faithfulness: Every directional prediction failed (herding 0.73 and 1.05 vs band 1.2-1.5; own-artifact #51 1.94, CI above 0.7; contrast has the wrong sign), and the synthetic shows the order is not identifiable once repos differ in fitness: p = 1 with fitness spread reproduces all estimates, and p = 0.5 reads as 1. C = 0, D = 0, H = 0; F = 1 for honest identification work.
rationale.usefulness: Mostly a negative instrument result: an operator cannot read winner-take-all dynamics from recruitment-vs-size slopes. The practical content (herding sits on kickoff-named repos; blind-window adoption is negligible at commit level; most recruitments are returns) restates H54 and H58.

one_line: Repo growth order is not identifiable from commit logs: first-order copying plus repo fitness spread explains every p-hat (0.7-1.9), and herding sits on kickoff-named repos.
